questions.question:
The statements below are followed by two conclusions labelled I and II. Assuming that the information in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with generally established facts, decide which conclusion(s) logically and definitely follow(s) from the information given in the statements.

**Statements:**

Some tents are cones.

All the cones are motels.

**Conclusions:**

All the motels are cones.

Some tents are motels.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/49c203e447e7ba0e5d16dd66b16ede4b0672cd445b3b919a553fe4a5e018c1a7.png] 

**Conclusions:**

1) All the motels are cones → All cones are motels which means some motels are cones, hence it is false.

2) Some tents are motels → True as shown in the above diagram.

Hence, only conclusion II follows.

questions.question:
In a shopping mall, five water bottles labelled as A, B, C, D and E were placed in a rack.

The bottle A has less price than the bottle B. The bottle C has less price than the bottle D. The bottle B has less price than the bottle C and bottle A has more price than the bottle E.

If a customer wants to buy a bottle of maximum price, then which bottle he/she has to buy?
questions.solution:
**5 Bottles:** A, B, C, D and E.

1) The bottle A has less price than the bottle B.

→ A < B

2) The bottle C has less price than the bottle D.

→ C < D

3) The bottle B has less price than the bottle C and bottle A has more price than the bottle E.

→ B < C,

→ E < A

On combining we get,

E < A < B < C < D

So, price of bottle D is higher than all other four bottles.

Hence, bottle D is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The statements below are followed by four conclusions labelled I, II, III and IV. Assuming that the information in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with generally established facts, decide which conclusion(s) logically and definitely follow(s) from the information given in the statements.

**Statements:**

No laptop is notebook.

All notebooks are tablets.

**Conclusions:**

I. No laptop is tablets.

II. No tablets is laptop.

III. Some tablets are notebooks.

IV. All the tablets are notebooks.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/506b520313506adaedfcad0ef2118c4e36e82f7399e7f0211a5616c0bd0cb14f.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. No laptop is tablets → It’s possible but not definite, hence false.

II. No tablets is laptop → It’s possible but not definite, hence false.

III. Some tablets are notebooks → All notebooks are tablets this means that some part of the tablets are notebook, hence true.

IV. All the tablets are notebooks → It’s not possible, hence false.

Hence, only conclusion III follows.

questions.question:
The statements given below are followed by two conclusions labelled I and II. Without resolving anything yourself, choose the conclusion which logically follows from the given statement.

**Statements:**

Most of the advocates are hard working.

Manoj is advocate.

**Conclusion I:** Manoj is politician.

**Conclusion II:** Some advocates do not work hard.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follows.
Both conclusion I and II follow

questions.solution:
The statement II mentions that Manoj is advocate but whether he is also a politician or not it can’t be concluded from the statement II. Thus, conclusion I does not follow.

Statement I mentions that most of the advocates are hard working which means that not all advocates are hard working. So, it can be concluded from the statement I that some advocates do not work hard. Thus, conclusion II follows.

Hence, only conclusion II follows.
